chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sayrafi al-Kufi narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us from Aban ibn Uthman al-Ahmar,

He said: I said to al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him): Inform me about Allah, Blessed and Exalted -- Has He always been All-Hearing, All-Seeing, All-Knowing, and All-Powerful? He said: Yes.

So I said to him: There is a man who claims allegiance to you, the Ahl al-Bayt, and he says: "Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has always been hearing through an instrument of hearing, seeing through sight, knowing through knowledge, and powerful through an instrument of power."

He said: So he (peace be upon him) became angry, then said: Whoever says that and takes it as his religion is a polytheist (mushrik), and has nothing to do with our authority (wilaya). Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is an Essence that is All-Knowing, All-Hearing, All-Seeing, and All-Powerful.

key_terms.ذات: Dhat -- Essence; the very being of God, as opposed to attributes conceived as separate entities.
key_terms.مشرك: Mushrik -- a polytheist; one who associates partners with God. Here used to condemn those who posit separate entities alongside God's essence.
key_terms.ولاية: Wilaya -- authority, guardianship, allegiance to the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt.

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about God's attributes being part of His essence?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Aban ibn Uthman al-Ahmar asks Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) about the divine attributes. The Imam confirms that God has eternally been Hearing, Seeing, Knowing, and Powerful. When told that someone claims God possesses these attributes through separate instruments or faculties (hearing through an organ of hearing, seeing through an organ of sight, etc.), the Imam becomes angry and declares such a person a polytheist who has no share in their authority. This teaching addresses the theological debate in early Islamic intellectual history about whether God's attributes are separate entities subsisting in His essence or are identical with His essence -- the Shia position being that God's attributes are His very essence, not external instruments added to it.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. `Ali Majiluwayh (rh) narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad b. Abi’l Qasim narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. `Ali al-Sayrafi al-Kufi narrated to me. He said: Muhammad b. Sinan narrated to us from Aban b. `Uthman al-Ahmar.
He said: I said to al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as): Inform me about Allah: Does He not cease in hearing, seeing, knowing, and being powerful? He said: Yes.

So, I said to him: There is a man who claims to be upon your wilaya, the Ahl al-Bayt, and he says: “Allah does not cease in seeing through sight, and hearing through [an instrument of] hearing, and knowing through knowledge, and being powerful through [an instrument of] power.”

So, he (as) became angry, then said: He who says this and takes his religion from this is a pagan that is not upon our wilaya in a thing. Surely, Allah is knowing, hearing, seeing, and powerful [without the aid of anything].
